exercises.why: **прошла** is the past tense (feminine) of **пройти** (to pass, to go, to walk; to pass by) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проходить**. past: он прошёл · она прошла́ · оно прошло́ · они прошли́. — Wiktionary, «пройти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **вышла** is the past tense (feminine) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. past: он вы́шел · она вы́шла · оно вы́шло · они вы́шли. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **выйти**: to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published; to spend, to be used up; to come off, to come out.  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «вы- — Step out for a short period of time: Секретарь вышел на десять минут. — The secretary left for ten minutes.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **сходятся** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **сходиться** (to meet, to come together; to converge, to coalesce) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **сойтись**. present: я схожу́сь · ты схо́дишься · он схо́дится · мы схо́димся · вы схо́дитесь · они схо́дятся. — Wiktionary, «сходиться» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со- (+сь, +ся)** — Convergent movement from various directions towards one center. Antonym: раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся) Example: Чтобы заниматься, студентка снесла все учебники из других комнат на письменный стол. — In order to study, the student brought all her textbooks from other rooms to her desk. Дети сбежались на детскую площадь. — The children ran (from all directions) to the playground. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **с-, со- (+сь, +ся)** — Convergent movement from various directions towards one center. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **провели** is the past tense (plural) of **провести** (to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проводить**. past: он провёл · она провела́ · оно провело́ · они провели́. — Wiktionary, «провести» (CC BY-SA 4.0). Note the expression: "проводить время" — to spend the time.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **провёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **провести** (to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проводить**. past: он провёл · она провела́ · оно провело́ · они провели́. — Wiktionary, «провести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **провести**: to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take; to lay, to construct, to build, to install a road, a pipe, a wire etc.; to carry out, to carry through, to realize, to put into practice, to conduct; to pass over, to run over.  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Проводить — провести — to lead through, to spend (time), to lay (a road). Note the expression: "проводить время" — to spend the time.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **прошли** is the past tense (plural) of **пройти** (to pass, to go, to walk; to pass by) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проходить**. past: он прошёл · она прошла́ · оно прошло́ · они прошли́. — Wiktionary, «пройти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **зашли** is the past tense (plural) of **зайти** (to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заходить**. past: он зашёл · она зашла́ · оно зашло́ · они зашли́. — Wiktionary, «зайти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **зайти**: to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch; (nautical) to call at, to enter (a port); (nautical) to get, to advance.  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
